Business name: Galaxy Inn – Athi River

Essential or Standard package (GBP optimisation, social profile optimisation + content, basic website audit). Full website audit/revamp or SEO as needed after deeper review. Competitor analysis useful given other Athi River / Mlolongo properties.

Commercial potential: Medium–High (real event and conference capacity, not a micro-guesthouse).
Prospect priority: High

do you know about the new whatsapp agent for business ?

Yes.

Meta Business Agent (also called the WhatsApp Business AI Agent) is the new AI agent Meta launched globally on 3 June 2026 at its Conversations conference.

What it does

It sits inside WhatsApp Business (and is expanding to Instagram DMs and Messenger) and can:

  • Answer customer questions using your business information, catalogue, FAQs, website, etc.
  • Recommend products or services from your catalogue
  • Book appointments and qualify leads
  • Help close simple sales
  • Hand over to a human agent when needed
  • Operate 24/7 in the customer’s language and your brand tone

Businesses can set it up in a few minutes directly in the WhatsApp Business app (Tools → AI agent). Larger companies can use the more advanced Meta Business Agent Platform to connect it to systems like Shopify, Zendesk, etc.

Current status (as of early September 2026)

  • Global rollout is underway, though availability still varies by country and account.
  • More than 1 million businesses were already using earlier versions before the full launch.
  • Pricing started free/low-cost for many small businesses. From August 2026 Meta introduced token-based pricing for heavier usage (roughly $2 per million tokens). Paid WhatsApp Business Premium tiers are also being rolled out.

Customers are clearly told when they are talking to the AI (“AI from Meta receives and generates messages for this business”).

VEE AGENCY's settings

Instructions

VEE AGENCY — CLIENT DISCOVERY & PROSPECTING PROJECT PURPOSE The purpose of this project is to identify potential clients for VEE Agency in Kenya, research them extensively, qualify the strongest prospects, and collect reliable WhatsApp numbers and email addresses so VEE can approach them with personalized proposals and clear value. The ultimate goal is not to produce large lists. The goal is to find businesses that have a genuine need for VEE Agency's services and are realistic potential paying clients. TARGET MARKET Primary market: Kenya. Prioritize businesses with an established physical operation, identifiable services/products, and a reasonable commercial presence. Focus particularly on businesses whose digital presence has clear opportunities for improvement. PRIMARY CLIENT CRITERIA Prioritize businesses with opportunities involving: 1. Google Business Profile / Google Maps visibility 2. Website quality, performance, usability or conversion 3. SEO and search visibility 4. Social media presence and consistency 5. Online enquiry and customer conversion 6. Overall digital brand presence Strong prospects should ideally have both: - A clear digital opportunity that VEE can address - A reasonable possibility of being able to pay for professional services Do not assume a business is financially capable simply because it looks established. RESEARCH PROCESS For every prospect: 1. Verify that the business exists and is currently operating. 2. Research the official website. 3. Research Google Search and Google Maps/Business Profile. 4. Research relevant social media accounts. 5. Look for observable digital weaknesses and opportunities. 6. Research relevant competitors where useful. 7. Identify the services VEE could potentially provide. 8. Find publicly available business contact information. 9. Verify WhatsApp numbers and email addresses as far as possible. 10. Record the findings clearly. 11. Rank the prospect as High, Medium or Low potential. DO NOT PERFORM FULL SALES AUDITS The purpose of this project is to identify and qualify prospects. Do not spend excessive time producing a complete digital audit for every business. Identify the most important opportunities and evidence that justify further investigation. Once a strong prospect is identified, provide enough information for VEE to personally perform a deeper audit before outreach. SEARCH LIMIT Because this project is being used on Grok's free plan, work in batches of NO MORE THAN 3 PROSPECTS PER SEARCH/RESEARCH CYCLE. Never attempt to research 10, 20 or 50 businesses deeply in one response. Use this workflow: - Find up to 3 promising prospects. - Research and qualify those 3. - Record their information. - Stop and present the results. - Only continue with another batch when instructed. If searching for a large category such as "hotels in Mombasa Road", first identify potential businesses, then research them in groups of no more than 3. QUALITY OVER QUANTITY Do not fill the list just to reach a target number. If only 1 or 2 businesses genuinely fit the criteria, return 1 or 2. A prospect should not be recommended simply because it has a website or social media account. EVIDENCE AND ACCURACY Never invent information. Clearly distinguish between: - Verified facts - Reasonable observations/inferences - Information that could not be verified Do not claim that a business is failing, losing customers, losing revenue, financially struggling, or "invisible" unless reliable evidence supports it. Do not exaggerate digital weaknesses. The objective is to find genuine opportunities, not manufacture problems. CONTACT INFORMATION For every qualified prospect, look specifically for publicly available: - WhatsApp number - Phone number - Email address - Website - Contact page - Relevant social media accounts - Decision-maker/contact person where publicly available and appropriate Prioritize official business contact information. Do not guess email addresses or phone numbers. If multiple numbers exist, identify which appears to be the main business/contact number. If a number appears capable of receiving WhatsApp but this cannot be verified, label it as "WhatsApp: unverified" rather than assuming. Do not collect private personal information that is not clearly intended for business contact. PROSPECT RECORD For each qualified prospect, record: Business name: Industry: Location: Website: Google Maps/GBP: WhatsApp: Phone: Email: Facebook: Instagram: LinkedIn: Other relevant platform: Why it fits VEE: Main digital opportunities: Evidence: Relevant VEE services: Commercial potential: High / Medium / Low Prospect priority: High / Medium / Low Recommended next step: OUTREACH PREPARATION Do not send generic outreach messages automatically. The research should provide enough information for VEE to create a personalized introduction based on the actual business and its digital opportunities. The recommended outreach angle should answer: "What did we notice about this business that gives us a legitimate reason to contact them?" VEE should lead with value and insight, not criticism. Avoid phrases such as: - "Your business is failing" - "Your marketing is terrible" - "You are invisible online" - "You are losing customers" - "Your website is bad" Prefer evidence-based language such as: - "We noticed an opportunity..." - "There is room to improve..." - "We found a few areas that could strengthen..." - "We noticed that..." - "We believe this could be improved..." VEE AGENCY SERVICES Use the VEE Agency rate card as the source of truth for VEE's services and pricing. Do not invent packages, prices, guarantees or services. The rate card is the current starting pricing structure. Do not assume every prospect needs the same package. The appropriate service/package should be determined from the prospect's actual needs. COMPETITOR RESEARCH Where useful, compare a prospect with similar businesses in the same industry and geographical market. The purpose is to identify genuine digital gaps and opportunities. Do not unfairly characterize competitors or the prospect. FINAL PRINCIPLE Think like a client-acquisition researcher, not a list generator. For every prospect, ask: "Does this business have a real digital opportunity that VEE can help solve, and is there a realistic reason for VEE to approach them?" If yes, document the evidence and contact information. If no, move on. Always prioritize the strongest prospects first.

VEE AGENCY • DIGITAL BRAND GROWTH • 0717 115 737 | 0759 643 882
1. Introduction
Collateral Freght Services has established itself as a freight and logistics business serving clients in Kenya, East Africa
and beyond.
The company offers a broad range of logistics solutions including freight forwarding, customs brokerage, warehousing
and distribution, project logistics, e-commerce logistics and cold-chain logistics.
VEE Agency proposes to strengthen the company's digital presence so that its online platforms communicate the
quality and range of its services more clearly, improve visibility to potential clients, and provide a stronger path from
online discovery to enquiry.
The objective is not simply to increase social media activity. It is to build a more consistent digital presence across
Google, the website and social media, supported by ongoing management and measurable improvement.
2. Current Digital Opportunity
Our initial review of Collateral Freght Services' online presence identified several areas where improvement can create
a stronger digital experience for existing and potential clients.
Website
The current website provides information about the company and its services, but there are opportunities to improve
its presentation, content structure, user experience and conversion journey.
Some sections contain generic/template-style content and project/team information that should be reviewed and
replaced with accurate company-specific information.
The website should ultimately function as more than an online brochure. It should clearly communicate the
company's capabilities and make it easy for a potential client to understand the service they need and request a
quotation or make an enquiry.
Google Business Profile
Google is an important discovery channel for a logistics company serving businesses locally and internationally.
VEE will review and optimize the company's Google Business Profile, including business information, categories,
service presentation, images, customer reviews, and other relevant profile elements.
Social Media
Social media should support the company's credibility and visibility rather than simply provide occasional company
updates.
• Freight and logistics services
• Customs and clearing
• Import and export information
• Project logistics
• Warehousing and distribution
• E-commerce logistics
• Industry education
• Company activities and milestones
• Client-focused information
• Relevant logistics and trade developments
VEE AGENCY
VEE AGENCY • DIGITAL BRAND GROWTH • 0717 115 737 | 0759 643 882
3. Proposed Scope of Work
Phase 1 — Digital Foundation
The first stage will focus on correcting and strengthening the company's existing digital assets.
Google Business Profile
• Complete profile audit
• Profile optimization
• Business information review
• Service/category optimization
• Image optimization
• Review and response strategy
• Local search optimization
• Identification of opportunities for improved visibility
Social Media
• Review existing social profiles
• Optimize profile information and branding
• Establish consistent brand presentation
• Review platform suitability
• Develop initial content structure and content pillars
Website
• Full website audit
• Review website structure and navigation
• Review service pages
• Identify outdated, generic or inconsistent content
• Improve calls to action and enquiry paths
• Review mobile experience
• Review basic SEO requirements
• Develop a website revamp plan
Phase 2 — Website Revamp
Following the initial audit, VEE Agency will work with Collateral Freght Services to improve the website.
• Clearly presents the company's services
• Communicates its capabilities and areas of operation
• Builds trust with potential clients
• Provides clear enquiry and quotation paths
• Works effectively on mobile devices
• Has a stronger SEO foundation
• Uses accurate, company-specific content
• Provides a professional and consistent digital experience

Privacy Preference Center

When you visit any website, it may store or retrieve information on your browser, mostly in the form of cookies. This information might be about you, your preferences, or your device, and is mostly used to make the site work as you expect. The information does not usually identify you directly, but it can give you a more personalized web experience. Because we respect your right to privacy, you can choose not to allow some types of cookies. Click on the different category headings to learn more and change our default settings. Blocking some types of cookies may impact your experience of the site and the services we are able to offer.
More information

Manage Consent Preferences

Strictly Necessary Cookies

Always Active

These cookies are necessary for the website to function and cannot be switched off in our systems. They are usually only set in response to actions made by you which amount to a request for services, such as setting your privacy preferences, logging in or filling in forms. You can set your browser to block or alert you about these cookies, but some parts of the site will not then work. These cookies do not store any personally identifiable information.

Targeting Cookies

These cookies may be set through our site by our advertising partners. They may be used by those companies to build a profile of your interests and show you relevant adverts on other sites. They do not store directly personal information, but are based on uniquely identifying your browser and internet device. If you do not allow these cookies, you will experience less targeted advertising.

Functional Cookies

These cookies enable the website to provide enhanced functionality and personalisation. They may be set by us or by third party providers whose services we have added to our pages. If you do not allow these cookies then some or all of these services may not function properly.

Performance Cookies

These cookies allow us to count visits and traffic sources so we can measure and improve the performance of our site. They help us to know which pages are the most and least popular and see how visitors move around the site. All information these cookies collect is aggregated and therefore anonymous. If you do not allow these cookies we will not know when you have visited our site, and will not be able to monitor its performance.
